import type { Improvement, ImprovementTree, Library } from './types.js';
import { GM_REFERENCE } from './seedGmReference.js';

/**
 * Content library seed data, ported verbatim from design/_shared/library.js.
 * Everything here is a *definition*; character sheets reference these by Id and never copy
 * them, so an admin-panel edit reaches every sheet on next render.
 */

/** Bump this whenever the content returned by `seedLibrary()` below changes. `runSeedIfEmpty()`
 *  only seeds an empty database, so a live library never picks up a seed edit on its own — the
 *  live library staying 16 releases stale went undetected for months (HANDOFF.md open issue 19).
 *  This gets stamped onto every seeded/reset `Library.SeedVersion`, so the live row can be compared
 *  against this constant to detect that drift automatically instead of relying on someone
 *  remembering to diff the two by hand. Any string works; matching the app version this content
 *  last changed in keeps it self-documenting. */
export const SEED_VERSION = '0.63.0';

/** The 25 Hero Improvement Trees (11 Combat + 14 Narrative), named and themed directly from
 *  Ruleset-V0.5.md's "Hero Improvements" section — real, authored content, unlike the
 *  placeholder nodes built on top of them below. "Command" is named twice in the doc (once per
 *  category) — kept as two distinct trees with the same display Name, disambiguated by Category,
 *  rather than merged into one. */
const IMPROVEMENT_TREE_DEFS: { id: string; name: string; category: 'Combat' | 'Narrative'; description: string }[] = [
  { id: 'it-strike', name: 'Strike', category: 'Combat', description: 'Direct attacks, signature weapons, and straightforward harm.' },
  { id: 'it-smash', name: 'Smash', category: 'Combat', description: 'Overwhelming force, wide destruction, and broken obstacles.' },
  { id: 'it-exploit', name: 'Exploit', category: 'Combat', description: 'Ambushes, marks, counters, and weak points.' },
  { id: 'it-control', name: 'Control', category: 'Combat', description: 'Restraint, forced movement, fear, terrain, and denial.' },
  { id: 'it-maneuver', name: 'Maneuver', category: 'Combat', description: 'Charges, retreats, leaps, flight, teleportation, and repositioning.' },
  { id: 'it-guard', name: 'Guard', category: 'Combat', description: 'Armor, shields, wards, parries, and interposition.' },
  { id: 'it-endure', name: 'Endure', category: 'Combat', description: 'Durability, resistance, recovery, and refusing defeat.' },
  { id: 'it-support', name: 'Support', category: 'Combat', description: 'Healing, cleansing, empowerment, and practical aid.' },
  { id: 'it-command-combat', name: 'Command', category: 'Combat', description: 'Formations, morale, coordination, and directing allies.' },

const SEED_IMPROVEMENT_TREES: ImprovementTree[] = IMPROVEMENT_TREE_DEFS.map((t) => ({ Id: t.id, Name: t.name, Category: t.category, Description: t.description }));

/** Ruleset-V0.5.md names all 25 trees above but never authors a single node on any of them — no
 *  Starting Improvement, no prerequisite line, nothing (see HANDOFF.md open issue 12). Rather
 *  than invent real mechanical effects that don't exist in the source document, each tree gets
 *  exactly two clearly-labeled placeholder nodes (a Starting Improvement and one node chained to
 *  it) — enough to exercise the DAG gate (`improvementState` in `logic.ts`) and the admin
 *  validation (`validateImprovementDag` in `adminLogic.ts`) end to end. Replace these with real
 *  authored content once the repo owner writes it; nothing else in this slice depends on their
 *  Effect text being real. */
const PLACEHOLDER_IMPROVEMENT_EFFECT = 'Placeholder — Ruleset-V0.5.md names this tree but has not authored its Improvements yet. This node only exists to exercise the prerequisite DAG; replace with real content (see HANDOFF.md open issue 12).';

const SEED_IMPROVEMENTS: Improvement[] = IMPROVEMENT_TREE_DEFS.flatMap((t) => {
  const startId = `im-${t.id.slice(3)}-1`;
  const nextId = `im-${t.id.slice(3)}-2`;
  return [
    { Id: startId, TreeId: t.id, Name: `${t.name} I (Starting, placeholder)`, Effect: PLACEHOLDER_IMPROVEMENT_EFFECT, IsStarting: true, PrerequisiteIds: [] },
    { Id: nextId, TreeId: t.id, Name: `${t.name} II (placeholder)`, Effect: PLACEHOLDER_IMPROVEMENT_EFFECT, IsStarting: false, PrerequisiteIds: [startId] },
  ];
});

>       { Id: 'm-camp', Name: 'Make Camp', Kind: 'Adventure', VirtueId: null, Description: 'While on an Adventure, 
when you are in a place of relative safety and decide to spend time together to rest or unwind, Make Camp. This can 
last for a few hours, a night, or a few days. While at Camp, all party members have +1 Ongoing to all +Heart rolls; 
perhaps making it a good time to open up to each other or discuss recent events.\n\nFirst, the GM advances the 
Adventure's Countdown. They do this once immediately and then, for every full day that dawns at this Camp, they may 
advance either the Adventure's Countdown or another Threat's Clock. When they do this, they may or may not disclose 
what has changed.\n\nThen, if anyone has at least 5 Potential on a Motif, any two Heroes have at least 5 Bond, or the 
Party has at least 5 Rapport, you may Advance a Motif, Progress the Party, or Forge a Bond. If you have enough, you 
can do any of these more than once.\n\nAll party members then do all of the following. In fiction these happen over 
their time at Camp. Play these out as you see fit: clear one Condition; Recuperate; refresh all Armor.\n\nNow, each 
Hero can take Camp Actions equal to the amount of Party Improvements. Camp Actions: rewrite or update any one of your 
Skill or Flaw Tags for the Party Motif to better reflect your Party as they are now; rewrite or update any one of your 
Skill or Flaw Tags for a Motif to better reflect your Hero as they are now; if both Heroes agree their Connection Tag 
no longer describes them, rewrite it and mark a Bond; use any relevant Party Improvement; progress a Project 
Clock.\n\nAfter all of this is done, if your Camp is somewhere potentially dangerous or vulnerable, before heading out 
on the next leg of your journey, the Party can decide to Keep Watch.', Results: { Tier3: { Description: 'No roll. Camp 
always works - the question is what it costs you in time.', Options: [], ChooseCount: 0 }, Tier2: { Description: '-', 
Options: [], ChooseCount: 0 }, Tier1: { Description: '-', Options: [], ChooseCount: 0 } } },
>       { Id: 'm-session', Name: 'End the Session', Kind: 'Adventure', VirtueId: null, Description: 'When you finish a

we uncover something new about the world? Did we save someone or something from certain doom? Did we learn something

strides to accomplish our Party Quest? If 1-2 answers are yes, mark 1 Rapport, if 3+ are yes, mark 2 Rapport.\n\nNext, 
each player chooses one of the following ways to grow: Grow closer with a Hero: Choose one Party member you've grown 
closer to and explain why. Mark a Bond between the two of you. Grow into your changes: Rewrite or update one of your 
Skill or Flaw Tags for a single Motif to better reflect who your Hero is now. Grow toward your goal: Mark one 
Potential on a Hero Motif whose Quest you actively progressed this session.', Results: { Tier3: { Description: 'No

>       { Id: 'm-aid', Name: 'Aid', Kind: 'Adventure', VirtueId: null, Description: 'Anyone in the Party can Aid

>       { Id: 'm-journey', Name: 'Set Out', Kind: 'Adventure', VirtueId: null, Description: 'When you gather your

>       { Id: 'm-downtime', Name: 'Enjoy Downtime', Kind: 'Adventure', VirtueId: null, Description: 'When you spend a

>       { Id: 'm-camp', Name: 'Make Camp', Kind: 'Adventure', VirtueId: null, Description: 'While on an Adventure,

    glossary: [
      { Id: 'g-condition', Name: 'Condition', Aliases: ['Conditions'], Definition: 'A marked penalty tied to one of your five Virtues - Exhausted (Might), Afraid (Mettle), Guilty (Heart), Angry (Wit), Insecure (Guile).       { Id: 'g-hero-roll', Name: 'Hero Roll', Aliases: ['Hero Rolls'], Definition: 'Roll 2d6 and add the relevant Virtue. Add +1 for one relevant Skill Tag and -1 for every relevant Flaw Tag.       { Id: 'g-misfortune', Name: 'Misfortune', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The GM's currency. At the beginning of a Session, if the GM has none, they gain 1.       { Id: 'g-hard-move', Name: 'Hard Move', Aliases: ['Hard Moves'], Definition: 'A GM move that gives the Heroes no time to react: it afflicts them with a tangible penalty, in the fiction or directly (marking Strain or a Condition), and the stakes meaningfully change.       { Id: 'g-soft-move', Name: 'Soft Move', Aliases: ['Soft Moves'], Definition: 'A GM move that threatens danger or pushes the Heroes toward a choice, while leaving them time to stop or divert it - often a setup ending in "What do you do?" A Soft Move can telegraph a later Hard Move.' },
      { Id: 'g-rapport', Name: 'Rapport', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A party-wide track marked when a move tells you to "mark Rapport." Filling it clears the track and raises Party Level by 1 - see Improvement. Rapport can also be spent directly as Aid - see Aid.' },
      { Id: 'g-work-together', Name: 'Work Together', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When any number of Heroes want to work as a group, the GM may ask for the Party to make a single Hero Roll to determine the outcome of a Move where the Party is acting as one.       { Id: 'g-party-quest', Name: 'Party Quest', Aliases: ['Party Quests'], Definition: 'What your group all must seek together - your reason for traveling as one rather than individuals.       { Id: 'g-motif', Name: 'Motif', Aliases: ['Motifs'], Definition: 'One of the three core aspects of your Hero - each a bucket for its own Skill Tags, Flaw Tags, a Potential track, and a Quest.       { Id: 'g-skill-tag', Name: 'Skill Tag', Aliases: ['Skill Tags'], Definition: 'A freeform word or phrase under a Motif describing something your Hero is good at.       { Id: 'g-flaw-tag', Name: 'Flaw Tag', Aliases: ['Flaw Tags'], Definition: 'A freeform word or phrase under a Motif describing a limit or weakness. A relevant Flaw Tag gives -1 to the roll, and acting on it marks Potential on that Motif whether the roll succeeds or fails.' },
      { Id: 'g-quest', Name: 'Quest', Aliases: ['Quests'], Definition: 'A short, player-written goal hanging off one Motif, tracked with three Act Breaks and three Forsakes. Three Act Breaks complete it; three Forsakes abandon it.' },
      { Id: 'g-potential', Name: 'Potential', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A track on each Motif, marked when a move tells you to "mark Potential" (or when you act on a Flaw Tag).       { Id: 'g-improvement', Name: 'Improvement', Aliases: ['Improvements', 'Improvement Tree', 'Hero Improvement'], Definition: 'A permanent pick taken off one of 25 Hero Improvement Trees (11 Combat, 14 Narrative) when a full Motif Potential track clears. Each Improvement can only be taken once. Party Improvements are named in the rules the same way but have no authored trees yet.' },
      { Id: 'g-hold', Name: 'Hold', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A pool of uses granted by a Move on a strong hit and spent one at a time until it runs out. Assess the Situation and Discern the Truth grant it; spend it to refresh a piece of Gear, clear a Condition, mark a Bond, or mark Potential.' },
      { Id: 'g-load', Name: 'Load', Aliases: [], Definition: 'How much you can carry. Each Item has a Load cost (0, 1, or 2); your total carried Load is capped by your Light/Normal/Heavy tier.' },
      { Id: 'g-bond', Name: 'Bond', Aliases: ['Bonds', 'Mark Bond', 'Bond Track', 'Bond Level'], Definition: 'How deeply a Connection between two Heroes runs, measured on its Bond Track. Mark 1 Bond when your Connection Tag meaningfully influences an important choice, creates a significant complication, or helps the two of you overcome a great obstacle together (once per Connection per scene), or when a move tells you to "mark Bond". At 5 Bond, the next time you Make Camp, the pair Forge a Bond: reduce the Bond Track by 5 and gain a Connection Improvement. Either Hero may spend a Bond at any time to influence the other. Marking Bond and Forging go through a propose/accept/reject handshake between the two players; spending Bond applies immediately.' },
      { Id: 'g-connection', Name: 'Connection', Aliases: ['Connections', 'Connection Tag', 'Connection Tags'], Definition: "Each pair of Heroes has one Connection, with a Connection Tag the two agree on that describes where their relationship stands now - pick one of the ruleset's examples or write your own.       { Id: 'g-status', Name: 'Status', Aliases: ['Statuses'], Definition: 'A named, lasting injury held in one of three severity slots - Minor (x3), Major (x2), or Severe (x1). Only the highest-severity Status you hold ever penalizes a roll: Minor is -1, Major is Disadvantage, Severe means rolling 1d6 instead of 2d6. Distinct from Strain (a short-term track that clears at the end of a scene) and from a Condition (always one of the five Virtue-linked penalties). Reduced by Recuperating, or downgraded a severity when your Healing Track fills.' },
      { Id: 'g-strain', Name: 'Strain', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A 5-box short-term harm track that clears completely at the end of the scene or Combat in which it was taken. Mark the box equal to an incoming amount, or the next unmarked box to its right. Resist an incoming amount by rolling + a Virtue to reduce it, or by choosing to take a Status instead (which absorbs a flat 2/4/6 by severity). Armor negates Strain entirely, up to its own limit.' },
      { Id: 'g-healing-track', Name: 'Healing Track', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A 5-segment track advanced by Recuperating (+Mettle: 3/2/1 segments by tier).       { Id: 'g-boon', Name: 'Boon', Aliases: ['Boons'], Definition: 'An unranked, freeform situational tag working in your favor - cleared the moment it stops being true. Compared against your Banes on a roll: more relevant Boons than Banes gives Advantage. See Advantage.' },
      { Id: 'g-bane', Name: 'Bane', Aliases: ['Banes'], Definition: 'An unranked, freeform situational tag working against you - cleared the moment it stops being true. Compared against your Boons on a roll: more relevant Banes than Boons gives Disadvantage. See Advantage.' },
      { Id: 'g-immobilized', Name: 'Immobilized', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A special Bane representing anything that prevents voluntary movement: grappling, paralysis, restraints, or binding magic. While Immobilized your Speed is 0 and you cannot move voluntarily, Maneuver, or Shift, but you may take other actions and forced movement can still move you. A Boon may cancel its effect on a roll but does not restore your movement. It ends when its fictional cause disappears or when someone successfully uses Break.' },
      { Id: 'g-crumble', Name: 'Crumble', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When you need to mark a Condition but all of them are already marked, you Crumble: you lose consciousness, flee, or otherwise must leave the scene. If you Crumble in Combat, you can only take actions that result in you fleeing or avoiding the action.' },
      { Id: 'g-subdued', Name: 'Subdued', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When a Hero must mark Strain but has no Strain box and does not prevent the Strain by taking a Status or using Armor, they are Subdued: they cannot continue the conflict, and the player and GM describe how they are removed from immediate danger - knocked unconscious, pinned, captured, separated, or forced to retreat. Subdual does not kill a Hero unless the player agrees that death is the appropriate outcome; what else happens is left to the table. An Enemy is Subdued when no legal Strain box remains (a Minion by any Move that inflicts at least 1 Strain), and the Hero who subdued it and the fiction decide whether it is unconscious, captured, routed, or killed.' },
      { Id: 'g-scar', Name: 'Scar', Aliases: ['Scars'], Definition: 'A near-permanent consequence a Hero can carry - a lost limb, a lingering nightmare, an unwanted transformation.       { Id: 'g-guard', Name: 'Guard', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Reduces the Strain inflicted on an Enemy by its value - Guard 1 by 1, Guard 2 by 2 - but never below 1 Strain, and it doesn't reduce Conditions or effects inflicted instead of Strain. Pierce ignores it. Guard should be visible in the fiction: a shield, a stone shell, a spectral barrier, impossible speed.' },
      { Id: 'g-pierce', Name: 'Pierce', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A Gambit: ignore the Enemy's Guard for this Move. See Guard.' },
      { Id: 'g-threat', Name: 'Threat', Aliases: ['Threat Level'], Definition: 'How many Heroes an Enemy is expected to occupy: � for a Minion, 1 Standard, 2 Elite, 4 Legendary. Add every Enemy's Threat and divide by the number of Heroes - Easy .5, Medium .75, Hard 1, Deadly 1.25, Very Deadly 1.5 or more. It is only a starting estimate.' },
      { Id: 'g-enemy-profile', Name: 'Enemy Profile', Aliases: ['Enemy Profiles', 'Minion', 'Minions', 'Elite', 'Legendary'], Definition: 'How much of a fight an Enemy is, which sets its defaults for Strain, Status slots and Conditions. A Minion (Threat �) is weak alone but dangerous in groups, and any Move that inflicts at least 1 Strain Subdues it; a Standard Enemy (Threat 1) can take on one Hero; an Elite (Threat 2) can take on two at once; a Legendary Enemy (Threat 4) fights the whole party, taking a turn after every Hero's turn. See Threat.' },
      { Id: 'g-last-stand', Name: 'Last Stand', Aliases: ['Bloodied'], Definition: 'A Legendary Enemy fights in three phases - Opening, Bloodied, then Last Stand (N) - each a five-box Strain track unless its stat block says otherwise.       { Id: 'g-range', Name: 'Range', Aliases: [], Definition: 'How far apart two combatants are: Melee, Close, Far, Very Far, or Out of Range. Maneuver and Shift move you between bands; Engage at Range and Engage in Melee each only work at their own band.' },
      { Id: 'g-aid', Name: 'Aid', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Spend 1 Rapport to give another Hero +1 on a roll, even after the dice are already rolled. You can Aid the same roll once per teammate, and Aid from multiple teammates stacks. Adding +1 this way cannot exceed +3 total on the roll.' },
      { Id: 'g-wealth', Name: 'Wealth', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A personal resource, freely adjusted on the sheet. Named sinks: spend 1 to roll Follow a Lead with Advantage, or during Enjoy Downtime to Rest, Carouse, Acquire, or Train.' },
      { Id: 'g-treasure', Name: 'Treasure', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A personal resource, freely adjusted on the sheet like Wealth. Ruleset-V0.6.md names no Wealth-distinct sink for Treasure any more - Carouse spends Wealth now - so it stays a freely adjusted resource with no automated hook.' },
      { Id: 'g-advantage', Name: 'Advantage', Aliases: ['Disadvantage'], Definition: 'Roll 3d6 and keep the best two (Advantage) or worst two (Disadvantage) instead of the usual 2d6 - decided by comparing your Boons and Banes relevant to the roll: more Boons is Advantage, more Banes is Disadvantage, a tie (including none of either) is Normal.       { Id: 'g-double-disadvantage', Name: 'Double Disadvantage', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The worst possible roll a Hero can make, arising from Repeated Attacks: roll 4d6 and keep the lowest two. This is the only rule that creates Double Disadvantage.' },
      { Id: 'g-repeated-attacks', Name: 'Repeated Attacks', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Whenever a Hero spends AP on a Move that can inflict Strain, count how many such Moves they have used since their AP last refreshed. A Move counts once however many creatures it targets, and a Reaction counts if it costs AP and can inflict Strain.' },
      { Id: 'g-prepare', Name: 'Prepare', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A Combat Move: your maximum AP becomes 4 during your next turn. Prepare does not stack with itself, and after that turn ends your maximum returns to normal.' },
      { Id: 'g-combat-goal', Name: 'Combat Goal', Aliases: ['Combat Goals'], Definition: 'The objective that must be achieved to end Combat, agreed on by the GM and Heroes when entering the Combat system. If the Heroes initiate Combat and all share the goal, they mark 1 Rapport.' },
      { Id: 'g-defiant-goal', Name: 'Defiant Goal', Aliases: ['Defiant Goals'], Definition: 'An alternative objective a minority of Heroes may declare during Combat if they disagree with the main Combat Goal.       { Id: 'g-consequence', Name: 'Consequence', Aliases: ['Burdened', 'Compromised', 'Delayed', 'Depleted', 'Exposed', 'Consequences'], Definition: 'One of five named outcomes on Invoke Expertise and Take a Risk: Burdened (a worse outcome, hard choice, or price to pay), Compromised (the situation escalates), Delayed (you take too long; things change meaningfully), Depleted (expend a resource or break a useful item), or Exposed (draw unwanted attention or leave a traceable trail).       { Id: 'g-camp-asset', Name: 'Camp Asset', Aliases: ['Camp Assets'], Definition: 'A magic item the party is afforded at creation to help them set up camp, leveling up through Tiers as the party progresses. Pick one from the library, or write your own on the spot.' },
      { Id: 'g-camp-action', Name: 'Camp Action', Aliases: ['Camp Actions'], Definition: 'One of the things each Hero may do at Make Camp: rewrite or update one of your Skill or Flaw Tags for the Party Motif, or for one of your Motifs; rewrite your Connection Tag, if both Heroes agree it no longer describes them, and mark a Bond; use any relevant Party Improvement; or progress a Project Clock.       { Id: 'g-push-yourself', Name: 'Push Yourself', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When more than one of your Skill Tags applies to a roll, mark one Condition to add a second +1 on top of your declared Skill Tag's own +1.' },
      { Id: 'g-set-out', Name: 'Set Out', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Gathering the party and venturing forth on the next leg of an Adventure - Choose your Loadout, then either simply arrive at a safe destination or Undertake a Perilous Journey through Scout Ahead and Venture Forth.       { Id: 'g-opposition-clock', Name: 'Opposition Clock', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The most common Clock - a Success track and a Failure track, both starting at 0 Headway.       { Id: 'g-threat-clock', Name: 'Threat Clock', Aliases: ['Threat Clocks'], Definition: 'A player-facing Clock for a brewing danger the Heroes have learned of - a Name, description, Goal, Skill Tags, and Developments (roughly one per segment), sized 2-4 for a nearby Threat, 4-6 regional, 7+ realm-spanning.       { Id: 'g-project-clock', Name: 'Project Clock', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A Hero's own downtime pursuit - building, crafting, enchanting, researching, and the like.       { Id: 'g-development', Name: 'Development', Aliases: ['Developments'], Definition: 'A planned consequence tied to one segment of a Threat Clock, triggered whenever it best serves the pacing rather than strictly in order - early Developments introduce the Threat lightly, later ones raise the stakes.' },
      { Id: 'g-headway', Name: 'Headway', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The amount (1-3) a Hero risks before rolling to progress an Opposition Clock - gained by the Heroes on a 10+, by both sides on a 7-9, or by the opposition alone on a 6-.' },
      { Id: 'g-villain', Name: 'Villain', Aliases: ['Villains'], Definition: 'The antagonist driving an Adventure's conflict - a monster, person, or anomaly with a Goal, a Scar, Skill Tags, Resources, Powers, Attacks, Resistances and Vulnerabilities, and Status Limits.       { Id: 'g-npc', Name: 'NPC', Aliases: ['NPCs', 'Non-Player Character'], Definition: 'A supporting-cast character with a Type (their function to you as a GM - Meddler, Minion, Gossip, Ally, Guard, Opportunist, Skeptic, Victim, or Witness), a Goal, and Skill Tags. Carouse: choose another involved Hero and describe a moment the two of you share, whether celebratory, consoling, or otherwise; mark Bond. Acquire: spend Wealth to procure new items and equipment available in town, repair your gear, refresh your stock, or acquire services. Train: spend 1 Wealth to mark Potential in a Motif of your choice. Pivot: change a Motif as if you had marked your third Forsake, or as a party decide to change or update the Party Motif. Pursue: party members can describe how they are starting or pursuing a long-term goal or project. For a new project, the GM and player define the Project Clock: give it a name, description, and how many segments it takes. Some projects may require other projects to be completed or special goals achieved before they can be attempted (GM discretion). Party members can work on the same project if they'd like, even if it was started by someone else. Examples of projects include building, crafting, enchanting, community service, and researching. Roll +an appropriate Virtue (see Results below). When everyone has finished enjoying downtime, they decide whether days, weeks, or months have passed; the GM then sets the next scene and progresses or starts a new Adventure Countdown and advances any Threats appropriately.', Results: { Tier3: { Description: 'Pursue marks 3 segments on the project's Clock. Every other activity above has no roll of its own.', Options: [], ChooseCount: 0 }, Tier2: { Description: 'Pursue marks 2 segments.', Options: [], ChooseCount: 0 }, Tier1: { Description: 'Pursue marks 1 segment.', Options: [], ChooseCount: 0 } } },
    ],
    glossary: [
      { Id: 'g-condition', Name: 'Condition', Aliases: ['Conditions'], Definition: 'A marked penalty tied to one of your five Virtues - Exhausted (Might), Afraid (Mettle), Guilty (Heart), Angry (Wit), Insecure (Guile). When you mark a Condition, you gain an associated Bane on any relevant roll until you clear it. Marking a Condition when all five are already marked means you Crumble.' },
      { Id: 'g-hero-roll', Name: 'Hero Roll', Aliases: ['Hero Rolls'], Definition: 'Roll 2d6 and add the relevant Virtue. Add +1 for one relevant Skill Tag and -1 for every relevant Flaw Tag. You may Push Yourself once per roll: mark a Condition and add +1 for a second relevant Skill Tag. The final modifier cannot exceed +3 or fall below -3. After determining the modifier, apply Advantage or Disadvantage from your Boons and Banes.' },
      { Id: 'g-misfortune', Name: 'Misfortune', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The GM's currency. At the beginning of a Session, if the GM has none, they gain 1. Whenever a Hero rolls 6-, in or out of Combat, the GM gains 1. The GM spends it 1 for 1 to make a Hard Move at any time, including immediately, and some GM and Enemy Moves cost Misfortune too. It carries over between Sessions and resets to 1 when an Adventure concludes.' },
      { Id: 'g-hard-move', Name: 'Hard Move', Aliases: ['Hard Moves'], Definition: 'A GM move that gives the Heroes no time to react: it afflicts them with a tangible penalty, in the fiction or directly (marking Strain or a Condition), and the stakes meaningfully change. The GM must spend a Misfortune to make one.' },
      { Id: 'g-soft-move', Name: 'Soft Move', Aliases: ['Soft Moves'], Definition: 'A GM move that threatens danger or pushes the Heroes toward a choice, while leaving them time to stop or divert it - often a setup ending in "What do you do?" A Soft Move can telegraph a later Hard Move.' },
      { Id: 'g-rapport', Name: 'Rapport', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A party-wide track marked when a move tells you to "mark Rapport." Filling it clears the track and raises Party Level by 1 - see Improvement. Rapport can also be spent directly as Aid - see Aid.' },
      { Id: 'g-work-together', Name: 'Work Together', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When any number of Heroes want to work as a group, the GM may ask for the Party to make a single Hero Roll to determine the outcome of a Move where the Party is acting as one. Each Hero may contribute one relevant Skill Tag, and any or all of the Party Tags may be used if they are relevant. All Hero's Flaw Tags may affect the roll as well, and the outcome affects the entire group.' },
      { Id: 'g-party-quest', Name: 'Party Quest', Aliases: ['Party Quests'], Definition: 'What your group all must seek together - your reason for traveling as one rather than individuals. It creates a path forward leading into Adventures and drives the story. Four varieties help define it: Vision (how the Party wants to change their world), Covenant (a binding vow or shared ideology), Shield (a realm or population to defend), or Expedition (a mystery or truth to uncover).' },
      { Id: 'g-motif', Name: 'Motif', Aliases: ['Motifs'], Definition: 'One of the three core aspects of your Hero - each a bucket for its own Skill Tags, Flaw Tags, a Potential track, and a Quest. You choose three Motifs at creation (from the thirteen suggested, or your own) and may rename any of them to fit your character.' },
      { Id: 'g-skill-tag', Name: 'Skill Tag', Aliases: ['Skill Tags'], Definition: 'A freeform word or phrase under a Motif describing something your Hero is good at. Declare a relevant Skill Tag before a roll to add +1; if more than one applies you may Push Yourself, mark a Condition, and add another +1.' },
      { Id: 'g-flaw-tag', Name: 'Flaw Tag', Aliases: ['Flaw Tags'], Definition: 'A freeform word or phrase under a Motif describing a limit or weakness. A relevant Flaw Tag gives -1 to the roll, and acting on it marks Potential on that Motif whether the roll succeeds or fails.' },
      { Id: 'g-quest', Name: 'Quest', Aliases: ['Quests'], Definition: 'A short, player-written goal hanging off one Motif, tracked with three Act Breaks and three Forsakes. Three Act Breaks complete it; three Forsakes abandon it.' },
      { Id: 'g-potential', Name: 'Potential', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A track on each Motif, marked when a move tells you to "mark Potential" (or when you act on a Flaw Tag). Filling a Motif's track clears it, raises Level by 1, and lets you add a Skill Tag, add or remove a Flaw Tag, or gain a Hero Improvement - see Improvement.' },
      { Id: 'g-improvement', Name: 'Improvement', Aliases: ['Improvements', 'Improvement Tree', 'Hero Improvement'], Definition: 'A permanent pick taken off one of 25 Hero Improvement Trees (11 Combat, 14 Narrative) when a full Motif Potential track clears. Each tree is its own small prerequisite chain: take a tree's Starting Improvement any time, or any other Improvement on that tree once you already hold one it connects to. Each Improvement can only be taken once. Party Improvements are named in the rules the same way but have no authored trees yet.' },
      { Id: 'g-hold', Name: 'Hold', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A pool of uses granted by a Move on a strong hit and spent one at a time until it runs out. Assess the Situation and Discern the Truth grant it; spend it to refresh a piece of Gear, clear a Condition, mark a Bond, or mark Potential.' },
      { Id: 'g-load', Name: 'Load', Aliases: [], Definition: 'How much you can carry. Each Item has a Load cost (0, 1, or 2); your total carried Load is capped by your Light/Normal/Heavy tier.' },
      { Id: 'g-bond', Name: 'Bond', Aliases: ['Bonds', 'Mark Bond', 'Bond Track', 'Bond Level'], Definition: 'How deeply a Connection between two Heroes runs, measured on its Bond Track. Mark 1 Bond when your Connection Tag meaningfully influences an important choice, creates a significant complication, or helps the two of you overcome a great obstacle together (once per Connection per scene), or when a move tells you to "mark Bond". At 5 Bond, the next time you Make Camp, the pair Forge a Bond: reduce the Bond Track by 5 and gain a Connection Improvement. Either Hero may spend a Bond at any time to influence the other. Marking Bond and Forging go through a propose/accept/reject handshake between the two players; spending Bond applies immediately.' },
      { Id: 'g-connection', Name: 'Connection', Aliases: ['Connections', 'Connection Tag', 'Connection Tags'], Definition: "Each pair of Heroes has one Connection, with a Connection Tag the two agree on that describes where their relationship stands now - pick one of the ruleset's examples or write your own. Bond is marked on it; at 5 Bond, the next time you Make Camp, the pair Forge a Bond: reduce the track by 5 and gain a Connection Improvement." },
      { Id: 'g-status', Name: 'Status', Aliases: ['Statuses'], Definition: 'A named, lasting injury held in one of three severity slots - Minor (x3), Major (x2), or Severe (x1). Only the highest-severity Status you hold ever penalizes a roll: Minor is -1, Major is Disadvantage, Severe means rolling 1d6 instead of 2d6. Distinct from Strain (a short-term track that clears at the end of a scene) and from a Condition (always one of the five Virtue-linked penalties). Reduced by Recuperating, or downgraded a severity when your Healing Track fills.' },
      { Id: 'g-strain', Name: 'Strain', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A 5-box short-term harm track that clears completely at the end of the scene or Combat in which it was taken. Mark the box equal to an incoming amount, or the next unmarked box to its right. Resist an incoming amount by rolling + a Virtue to reduce it, or by choosing to take a Status instead (which absorbs a flat 2/4/6 by severity). Armor negates Strain entirely, up to its own limit.' },
      { Id: 'g-healing-track', Name: 'Healing Track', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A 5-segment track advanced by Recuperating (+Mettle: 3/2/1 segments by tier). When it fills, every Status you hold drops one severity (renamed to reflect the improvement, where a slot is free at the lower severity) and the track clears, carrying any remaining segments onto the fresh one.' },
      { Id: 'g-boon', Name: 'Boon', Aliases: ['Boons'], Definition: 'An unranked, freeform situational tag working in your favor - cleared the moment it stops being true. Compared against your Banes on a roll: more relevant Boons than Banes gives Advantage. See Advantage.' },
      { Id: 'g-bane', Name: 'Bane', Aliases: ['Banes'], Definition: 'An unranked, freeform situational tag working against you - cleared the moment it stops being true. Compared against your Boons on a roll: more relevant Banes than Boons gives Disadvantage. See Advantage.' },
      { Id: 'g-immobilized', Name: 'Immobilized', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A special Bane representing anything that prevents voluntary movement: grappling, paralysis, restraints, or binding magic. While Immobilized your Speed is 0 and you cannot move voluntarily, Maneuver, or Shift, but you may take other actions and forced movement can still move you. A Boon may cancel its effect on a roll but does not restore your movement. It ends when its fictional cause disappears or when someone successfully uses Break.' },
      { Id: 'g-crumble', Name: 'Crumble', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When you need to mark a Condition but all of them are already marked, you Crumble: you lose consciousness, flee, or otherwise must leave the scene. Say how, then clear one Condition immediately, and discuss with the GM how and when you'll return. If you Crumble in Combat, you can only take actions that result in you fleeing or avoiding the action.' },
      { Id: 'g-subdued', Name: 'Subdued', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When a Hero must mark Strain but has no Strain box and does not prevent the Strain by taking a Status or using Armor, they are Subdued: they cannot continue the conflict, and the player and GM describe how they are removed from immediate danger - knocked unconscious, pinned, captured, separated, or forced to retreat. Subdual does not kill a Hero unless the player agrees that death is the appropriate outcome; what else happens is left to the table. An Enemy is Subdued when no legal Strain box remains (a Minion by any Move that inflicts at least 1 Strain), and the Hero who subdued it and the fiction decide whether it is unconscious, captured, routed, or killed.' },
      { Id: 'g-scar', Name: 'Scar', Aliases: ['Scars'], Definition: 'A near-permanent consequence a Hero can carry - a lost limb, a lingering nightmare, an unwanted transformation. The old Subdued-triggered choice that used to grant one (Take a Scar / Risk Death / Blaze of Glory) has been retired with no stated replacement; Scars themselves stay on the sheet as free text for whenever the table narrates one.' },
      { Id: 'g-guard', Name: 'Guard', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Reduces the Strain inflicted on an Enemy by its value - Guard 1 by 1, Guard 2 by 2 - but never below 1 Strain, and it doesn't reduce Conditions or effects inflicted instead of Strain. Pierce ignores it. Guard should be visible in the fiction: a shield, a stone shell, a spectral barrier, impossible speed.' },
      { Id: 'g-pierce', Name: 'Pierce', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A Gambit: ignore the Enemy's Guard for this Move. See Guard.' },
      { Id: 'g-threat', Name: 'Threat', Aliases: ['Threat Level'], Definition: 'How many Heroes an Enemy is expected to occupy: � for a Minion, 1 Standard, 2 Elite, 4 Legendary. Add every Enemy's Threat and divide by the number of Heroes - Easy .5, Medium .75, Hard 1, Deadly 1.25, Very Deadly 1.5 or more. It is only a starting estimate.' },
      { Id: 'g-enemy-profile', Name: 'Enemy Profile', Aliases: ['Enemy Profiles', 'Minion', 'Minions', 'Elite', 'Legendary'], Definition: 'How much of a fight an Enemy is, which sets its defaults for Strain, Status slots and Conditions. A Minion (Threat �) is weak alone but dangerous in groups, and any Move that inflicts at least 1 Strain Subdues it; a Standard Enemy (Threat 1) can take on one Hero; an Elite (Threat 2) can take on two at once; a Legendary Enemy (Threat 4) fights the whole party, taking a turn after every Hero's turn. See Threat.' },
      { Id: 'g-last-stand', Name: 'Last Stand', Aliases: ['Bloodied'], Definition: 'A Legendary Enemy fights in three phases - Opening, Bloodied, then Last Stand (N) - each a five-box Strain track unless its stat block says otherwise. When a phase can't mark incoming Strain, it ends and the rest of that Strain is discarded. It loses at most one phase between its own activations. Last Stand (N) clears the N highest-numbered marked boxes, which become its final capacity; when it can't mark Strain in Last Stand, it is Subdued.' },
      { Id: 'g-range', Name: 'Range', Aliases: [], Definition: 'How far apart two combatants are: Melee, Close, Far, Very Far, or Out of Range. Maneuver and Shift move you between bands; Engage at Range and Engage in Melee each only work at their own band.' },
      { Id: 'g-aid', Name: 'Aid', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Spend 1 Rapport to give another Hero +1 on a roll, even after the dice are already rolled. You can Aid the same roll once per teammate, and Aid from multiple teammates stacks. Adding +1 this way cannot exceed +3 total on the roll.' },
      { Id: 'g-wealth', Name: 'Wealth', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A personal resource, freely adjusted on the sheet. Named sinks: spend 1 to roll Follow a Lead with Advantage, or during Enjoy Downtime to Rest, Carouse, Acquire, or Train.' },
      { Id: 'g-treasure', Name: 'Treasure', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A personal resource, freely adjusted on the sheet like Wealth. Ruleset-V0.6.md names no Wealth-distinct sink for Treasure any more - Carouse spends Wealth now - so it stays a freely adjusted resource with no automated hook.' },
      { Id: 'g-advantage', Name: 'Advantage', Aliases: ['Disadvantage'], Definition: 'Roll 3d6 and keep the best two (Advantage) or worst two (Disadvantage) instead of the usual 2d6 - decided by comparing your Boons and Banes relevant to the roll: more Boons is Advantage, more Banes is Disadvantage, a tie (including none of either) is Normal. A Major Status is a separate source of Disadvantage the ruleset doesn't say how to combine with a Boon/Bane-driven one - both are shown, and the table resolves it. Double Disadvantage (from Repeated Attacks) is the worst possible roll: roll 4d6 and keep the lowest two.' },
      { Id: 'g-double-disadvantage', Name: 'Double Disadvantage', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The worst possible roll a Hero can make, arising from Repeated Attacks: roll 4d6 and keep the lowest two. This is the only rule that creates Double Disadvantage.' },
      { Id: 'g-repeated-attacks', Name: 'Repeated Attacks', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Whenever a Hero spends AP on a Move that can inflict Strain, count how many such Moves they have used since their AP last refreshed. Work out Advantage or Disadvantage from Boons and Banes as normal, then worsen the roll one step for each previous Strain-inflicting Move, as far as Double Disadvantage. A Move counts once however many creatures it targets, and a Reaction counts if it costs AP and can inflict Strain.' },
      { Id: 'g-prepare', Name: 'Prepare', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A Combat Move: your maximum AP becomes 4 during your next turn. Prepare does not stack with itself, and after that turn ends your maximum returns to normal.' },
      { Id: 'g-combat-goal', Name: 'Combat Goal', Aliases: ['Combat Goals'], Definition: 'The objective that must be achieved to end Combat, agreed on by the GM and Heroes when entering the Combat system. Examples include defeating the opposition, rescuing a prisoner, recovering an item, crossing a bridge, or escaping an area. If the Heroes initiate Combat and all share the goal, they mark 1 Rapport.' },
      { Id: 'g-defiant-goal', Name: 'Defiant Goal', Aliases: ['Defiant Goals'], Definition: 'An alternative objective a minority of Heroes may declare during Combat if they disagree with the main Combat Goal. Achieving a Defiant Goal allows only those Heroes to leave Combat. Combat ends for everyone only if the table agrees the Defiant Goal has superseded the main Goal.' },
      { Id: 'g-consequence', Name: 'Consequence', Aliases: ['Burdened', 'Compromised', 'Delayed', 'Depleted', 'Exposed', 'Consequences'], Definition: 'One of five named outcomes on Invoke Expertise and Take a Risk: Burdened (a worse outcome, hard choice, or price to pay), Compromised (the situation escalates), Delayed (you take too long; things change meaningfully), Depleted (expend a resource or break a useful item), or Exposed (draw unwanted attention or leave a traceable trail). Replaces the old Attrition/Detection/Danger/Delay/Sacrifice vocabulary.' },
      { Id: 'g-camp-asset', Name: 'Camp Asset', Aliases: ['Camp Assets'], Definition: 'A magic item the party is afforded at creation to help them set up camp, leveling up through Tiers as the party progresses. Pick one from the library, or write your own on the spot.' },
      { Id: 'g-camp-action', Name: 'Camp Action', Aliases: ['Camp Actions'], Definition: 'One of the things each Hero may do at Make Camp: rewrite or update one of your Skill or Flaw Tags for the Party Motif, or for one of your Motifs; rewrite your Connection Tag, if both Heroes agree it no longer describes them, and mark a Bond; use any relevant Party Improvement; or progress a Project Clock. Each Hero can take Camp Actions equal to the number of Party Improvements.' },
      { Id: 'g-push-yourself', Name: 'Push Yourself', Aliases: [], Definition: 'When more than one of your Skill Tags applies to a roll, mark one Condition to add a second +1 on top of your declared Skill Tag's own +1.' },
      { Id: 'g-set-out', Name: 'Set Out', Aliases: [], Definition: 'Gathering the party and venturing forth on the next leg of an Adventure - Choose your Loadout, then either simply arrive at a safe destination or Undertake a Perilous Journey through Scout Ahead and Venture Forth. Formerly named "Undertake a Journey."' },
      { Id: 'g-opposition-clock', Name: 'Opposition Clock', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The most common Clock - a Success track and a Failure track, both starting at 0 Headway. Risking 1-3 Headway before a roll: a 10+ adds the risked Headway to Success, a 7-9 adds it to both, a 6- adds it to Failure.' },
      { Id: 'g-threat-clock', Name: 'Threat Clock', Aliases: ['Threat Clocks'], Definition: 'A player-facing Clock for a brewing danger the Heroes have learned of - a Name, description, Goal, Skill Tags, and Developments (roughly one per segment), sized 2-4 for a nearby Threat, 4-6 regional, 7+ realm-spanning. A GM may promote one to the campaign\'s Quest Board. Advances by the GM\'s own hand, often at Make Camp - this app doesn\'t advance a neglected Threat on its own.' },
      { Id: 'g-project-clock', Name: 'Project Clock', Aliases: [], Definition: 'A Hero\'s own downtime pursuit - building, crafting, enchanting, researching, and the like. Give it a name, description, and Goal; progress it by rolling + an appropriate ability and reporting the tier (10+: 3 segments, 7-9: 2, 6-: 1), the same way Enjoy Downtime\'s Advance and a Camp Action already work.' },
      { Id: 'g-development', Name: 'Development', Aliases: ['Developments'], Definition: 'A planned consequence tied to one segment of a Threat Clock, triggered whenever it best serves the pacing rather than strictly in order - early Developments introduce the Threat lightly, later ones raise the stakes.' },
      { Id: 'g-headway', Name: 'Headway', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The amount (1-3) a Hero risks before rolling to progress an Opposition Clock - gained by the Heroes on a 10+, by both sides on a 7-9, or by the opposition alone on a 6-.' },
      { Id: 'g-villain', Name: 'Villain', Aliases: ['Villains'], Definition: 'The antagonist driving an Adventure's conflict - a monster, person, or anomaly with a Goal, a Scar, Skill Tags, Resources, Powers, Attacks, Resistances and Vulnerabilities, and Status Limits. A Villain doesn't need to be killed or even defeated to conclude an Adventure - their Goal only needs to be thwarted.' },
      { Id: 'g-npc', Name: 'NPC', Aliases: ['NPCs', 'Non-Player Character'], Definition: 'A supporting-cast character with a Type (their function to you as a GM - Meddler, Minion, Gossip, Ally, Guard, Opportunist, Skeptic, Victim, or Witness), a Goal, and Skill Tags. A Combatant NPC gets Status Limits, same as an Enemy.' },
      { Id: 'g-location', Name: 'Location', Aliases: ['Locations'], Definition: 'A place the Heroes are expected to spend time during an Adventure - 3 Aspects the Heroes can interact with, plus a Location Type (Nexus, Deathtrap, Lair, Citadel, Lab, Archive, Labyrinth, Gaol, or Wilds) describing its purpose.' },
      { Id: 'g-party-motif', Name: 'Party Motif', Aliases: [], Definition: 'The Motif the whole Party shares: why you travel together. It holds two Party Skill Tags and two Party Flaw Tags, and a Party Quest. Each Party Tag works for a single Hero Roll, then refreshes when the Party Makes Camp; invoking one marks Rapport.' },
      { Id: 'g-party-improvement', Name: 'Party Improvement', Aliases: ['Party Improvements'], Definition: 'An improvement the whole Party gains - one at creation, and more through Progress the Party. Each Hero may take as many Camp Actions as the Party has Party Improvements.' },
    ],

    /** Ruleset-V0.5.md never names an actual Camp Asset - only the generic concept ("a magic camp
     *  item that facilitates setting up their camp... it levels up as they progress into the
     *  tiers"). These three are illustrative starting examples, same spirit as the two seeded
     *  Enemies above; a party can also just write their own ad-hoc one at Camp (see
     *  `PartyCampAsset`). */
    campAssets: [
      { Id: 'ca-tent', Name: 'Ever-Warm Tent', Description: 'A canvas pavilion that pitches itself in minutes and holds the chill outside no matter the season.', Tier: 1, Effect: 'Camp always feels safe and comfortable, regardless of weather.' },
      { Id: 'ca-hearth', Name: 'Hearthstone', Description: 'A fist-sized stone that lights a fire from nothing and never needs fuel.', Tier: 1, Effect: 'Camp always has light and warmth, even with no wood to burn.' },
      { Id: 'ca-wardposts', Name: 'Warding Posts', Description: 'Four carved stakes that hum faintly when driven into the ground around a camp.', Tier: 2, Effect: 'Anything hostile approaching the camp perimeter announces itself - treat Keep Watch's 6- result as a 7-9 instead.' },
    ],
    /** Ruleset-V0.5.md's "Villains and Enemies in Combat" section gives exactly one worked example
     *  - Grizza the Tall - complete with Goal, flavor text, and a stat block (rewritten in the
     *  revised ruleset's format; `Stats` below); seeded here verbatim rather than invented. `Aspects`/`Scar`/`SkillTags`/`Resources`/
     *  `Powers`/`Attacks`/`Resistances`/`Vulnerabilities` fill in the doc's own "a Villain is
     *  comprised of" checklist from that same worked example's flavor text and the earlier Adventure
     *  Concept text ("a pack of goblins... steal the blacksmith's daughter... to cleanse the ancient
     *  tomb they've recently overtaken") - the doc doesn't spell every one of these fields out for
     *  Grizza by name, so this is a reasonable, clearly-attributed fill-in, not a second invented
     *  Villain. */
    villains: [
      {
        Id: 'vil-grizza',
        Name: 'Grizza the Tall',
        Aspects: ['Taller-Than-Average Goblin', 'Draped in Rotting Furs', 'Spider-Eyed Hat'],
        Goal: 'Prove her power to her new goblin clan and earn the family she never had, backed by a claimed connection to the divine Vuldec, Lord of Goblins.',
        Scar: 'Shunned by her own clan as a child, then watched its leaders turn even her friends against her - she has spent every day since proving she needs none of them.',
        SkillTags: ['Command Over Lesser Magic', 'Commands Fierce Loyalty', 'Never Forgets a Slight'],
        Resources: ['Her Goblin Clan', 'The Ancient Tomb They've Overtaken', 'Claimed Favor of Vuldec, Lord of Goblins', 'The Blacksmith's Captive Daughter'],
        Powers: 'Commands lesser magic - enough to convince a clan of goblins that she truly speaks for Vuldec.',
        Attacks: 'Fall to my Power! - closes to Melee and lashes out, dealing Wounded and Wobbly. Fearsome Yell - a deafening roar that rattles everyone nearby, dealing Deafened to all who hear it.',
        Resistances: 'Fear and intimidation alone don't rattle her - she's used to being underestimated.',
        Vulnerabilities: 'Her connection to Vuldec is a bluff; exposing it in front of her clan strips her authority instantly.',
